subsystems.name: Continuous glucose sensing
subsystems.role: measures glucose in subcutaneous fluid every few minutes and streams it wirelessly.

subsystems.name: Insulin pump and infusion set
subsystems.role: delivers rapid-acting insulin in small, precisely timed doses.

subsystems.name: Control algorithm
subsystems.role: forecasts glucose and decides how much insulin to deliver or withhold.

subsystems.name: User interface and connectivity
subsystems.role: lets the user announce meals, set temporary targets and receive alerts.

subsystems.name: Safety and fail-safe layer
subsystems.role: prevents overdosing and handles sensor or pump failure.
parts: maximum hourly and daily dose caps

subsystems.name: Insulin and site management
subsystems.role: the drug and subcutaneous route on which the loop depends.

buildSteps.title: Model glucose and insulin dynamics
buildSteps.detail: Clinical studies quantify sensor lag of roughly 5–15 minutes, insulin action over 30–60 minutes, and how much these vary between people and within a day.

buildSteps.title: Write the controller
buildSteps.detail: The algorithm forecasts glucose 30–60 minutes ahead, calculates a basal rate or micro-bolus, and subtracts insulin still active to avoid stacking doses.

buildSteps.title: Build the safety envelope
buildSteps.detail: Hard limits cap total insulin, suspend delivery when glucose is predicted to fall below about 3.9 mmol/L, and flag blocked tubing or a failed sensor.

buildSteps.title: Integrate devices
buildSteps.detail: CGM and pump communicate over a encrypted wireless link; the system must keep working or fail safe when a phone or sensor drops out.

buildSteps.title: Test in simulation and benchtop rigs
buildSteps.detail: Virtual patient populations and mechanical test rigs exercise meals, exercise, illness and sensor dropout before any human use.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Outpatient and overnight studies measure time in the 3.9–10.0 mmol/L range, hypoglycaemia and user burden against standard pump therapy.

buildSteps.title: Clear regulation and manufacture
buildSteps.detail: Software lifecycle records, sterile disposable infusion sets and traceable insulin reservoirs must meet medical-device quality systems.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with training and monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Users learn meal bolusing and alarm handling; remote data review and software updates keep the loop safe after launch.

prerequisites.why: the loop needs frequent, reliable glucose readings without fingersticks.
fast onset and predictable action let the controller correct high glucose quickly.
automated control requires accurate micro-dosing and a digital command link.

prerequisites.tech: Embedded control software and wireless security
prerequisites.why: the algorithm must run reliably on a battery-powered device and resist tampering.
current commercial systems still rely on the user counting carbohydrates and announcing meals.

pathway.milestone: commercial hybrid closed-loop systems automating basal insulin and corrections, especially overnight
pathway.unlocks: better time in range with less fear of nocturnal lows.

pathway.milestone: loops that handle unannounced meals and exercise with less user input
pathway.unlocks: closer to a fully closed loop for everyday life.

pathway.milestone: dual-hormone systems adding glucagon to counter lows
pathway.unlocks: tighter control without increasing hypoglycaemia risk.

pathway.milestone: implantable sensors and pumps, or cells that release insulin automatically
